domain: electricity, gas, water, pipelines, utilities, grid interconnection, public commissions, infrastructure finance, and large-load demand
jurisdictions: United States federal and state jurisdictions
scope: Regulated utilities, generators, transmission, pipelines, water systems, public utility commissions, FERC dockets, interconnection queues, rate cases, large-load and data-center demand, infrastructure finance, reliability, public subsidies, and ownership. The estate preserves docket, facility, utility, customer, capacity, rate, approval, construction, and operational dates.
why_new_estate: Compute, industrial policy, local development, public money, and defense manufacturing all terminate at power, water, pipeline, or grid constraints not owned by an existing estate.

denominator_contract.unit: one facility, utility docket, interconnection request, rate instrument, or public infrastructure project with exact identifiers
denominator_contract.inclusion_rule: FERC and state dockets, utility filings, EIA plant/load data, contracts, bonds, public agreements, and corporate ownership filings.
denominator_contract.exclusion_rule: Projected capacity as operating capacity; geographic proximity as shared infrastructure; rate approval as project completion.
jurisdictions: United States federal and state jurisdictions
denominator_contract.time_window: historical through 2026-07-23, with each source query recording its own bounded window

source_routes.bounded_output: FERC dockets, accession numbers, filings, issuances, orders, maps, forms, parties, document dates, filed dates, and posted dates.
source_routes.residual_fog: Docket metadata does not establish construction or operation; CEII, privileged, protected, legacy, and state-jurisdiction records may be unavailable.

source_routes.bounded_output: Electricity, plant, generator, balancing-authority, fuel, demand, flow, capacity, outage, and other energy time series and bulk files.
source_routes.residual_fog: EIA identifiers and reporting scope differ by dataset; proposed facilities, customer-specific load, ownership, and regulatory status require external joins.

source_routes.authority: United States state public utility commissions
source_routes.bounded_output: State rate cases, certificates, interconnection, utility filings, orders, service territories, and party records.
source_routes.residual_fog: Systems, identifiers, access, redactions, and historical coverage vary by commission; no single national docket denominator exists.

source_routes.bounded_output: Award and transaction identifiers with separate ceiling, obligation, and outlay fields.
source_routes.residual_fog: Recipient identity, award hierarchy, subaward coverage, and performance reconciliation remain estate-specific.

source_routes.authority: Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board and issuers
source_routes.bounded_output: Official statements, continuing disclosures, debt service, event notices, and CUSIP-linked documents.
source_routes.residual_fog: Bond proceeds, draws, reimbursements, issuer accounting, and project-level cash flows require issuer records and audits.

source_routes.authority: Municipal clerks, development agencies, and public authorities
source_routes.bounded_output: Executed development, incentive, infrastructure, lease, disposition, community-benefit, and amendment instruments.
source_routes.residual_fog: Agreements are distributed across clerks, boards, project sites, and records requests; summaries are not substitutes.

source_routes.bounded_output: CIKs, accession numbers, filing types, Form D offerings, ownership, merger, and company filings.
source_routes.residual_fog: CIK resolution, filer/entity boundaries, amended filings, and governance-right extraction require estate-specific parsing.

boundaries: A proposed project, queue position, rate filing, approval, financing, construction milestone, and operating asset are different states. Shared grid geography is not a relationship.
A surveyed and prepared estate is not an acquired, completed, or finding-bearing estate.
Official source availability is not evidence of a subject overlap.
